# Elias Manos

::: {.subtitle}
PhD Candidate in Natural Resources & the Environment · Geospatial Data Science · Arctic Infrastructure Risk · GeoAI · Satellite Earth Observation
:::
:::

I am a geospatial data scientist and PhD candidate at the University of Connecticut. My research combines satellite Earth observation, artificial intelligence, and spatial modeling to study Arctic infrastructure, settlement change, and climate risk.

My work develops scalable geospatial datasets and methods for data-scarce regions, with a focus on permafrost-affected communities and the built environment.

::: {.callout-box}
**Research focus:** GeoAI for Arctic built environments, permafrost infrastructure risk, settlement change, nighttime lights, and climate-driven impacts in data-scarce regions.
:::

## Current research themes

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.card}
### Arctic infrastructure risk
Estimating exposure and potential damage to buildings and infrastructure from permafrost degradation across Arctic regions.
:::

::: {.card}
### GeoAI and building detection
Developing deep learning methods to map building footprints and characterize infrastructure in remote, data-scarce environments.
:::

::: {.card}
### Settlement change
Using nighttime lights, population data, and remote sensing time series to study settlement decline, persistence, and transformation.
:::

:::

## Selected work

- Pan-Arctic building exposure and permafrost degradation damage modeling.
- Deep learning-based Arctic building footprint mapping.
- Nighttime lights analysis of Russian Arctic settlement change.
